points.why: Names Fixes That Fail and says the coupon relieves complaints but adds peak demand that worsens lateness.
Traces the quick-fix loop (complaint → coupon → fewer complaints) and the side-effect loop (coupons → peak demand → late deliveries → more complaints and coupons).
Calls 30% a bigger dose of the same fix and advises against it.
Recommends the coupon only as a bridge, fixing peak capacity, off-peak-only redemption, and tracking redemption by time slot and peak late-rate.

pitfalls.why: Uses Fixes That Fail correctly and never invokes Shifting the Burden.

notes: The experiment wording 'peak-only 30% group' is muddled, since the 30% coupon isn't restricted to peak, but this is minor.
